short: Sensors, HMM decoder and class grammar are all standard; the 8.9% WER is the authors' 2014 five of six subjects (2014 mean 11.2%), with no stated test split.
position: The paper [@meltzner2018development] changes an 11-site face and neck sEMG array with an exhaustive 2,047-subset search (M05), a Kaldi triphone HMM with HLDA, MLLR and SGMM (M06) and a hand-built natural-language class grammar (M07); all three are standard against the ledger, and the same pipeline, four task sets and subject rows were published by the same group in 2014 [@deng2014practical], uncited here. The headline 8.9% WER is the 2014 SGMM table with one of six subjects removed (2014 mean 11.2%); the 2,200-word figure is the corpus total while each test set held 88-167 words under a grammar derived from the corpus's own sentence rules, and no test partition is reported (M12), so "far surpassing previous attempts" rests on unmatched protocols.
